subject: bridge collapse

source_quote: The bridge cracked under her. Thorin's work. She leapt clear anyway.

subject: bridge collapse
fact: The bridge in Velkynvelve collapsed, a result of prolonged effort rather than strategy, allowing passage into the cavern below.
source_quote: The bridge going down was my idea, technically, but I can't take full credit for it feeling satisfying. You swing at a bridge long enough, the bridge falls.

subject: Bridge collapse
fact: Thorin destroyed the bridge, forcing Ilvara and Jorlan to fall into the cavern below; the collapse was a physical turning point that shifted the battle from vertical to horizontal, and symbolized the ruin of all structure — both architectural and moral.
source_quote: The bridge going down was my idea, technically, but I can't take full credit for it feeling satisfying.

subject: bridge collapse
fact: Thorin’s act of collapsing the bridge was a decisive, one-round event that ended positional advantage and forced combatants into the cavern below.
source_quote: Thorin had already toppled the bridge, sent both of them crashing to the cavern floor.

subject: critical strikes and drop

source_quote: Forty feet up, gripping a corrupted high priestess, delivering consecutive critical strikes — and then I let her go. That was the point.

subject: Daz

source_quote: I spent a moment noting the look on their faces. That specific expression — the slight recalibration when the target doesn't go down. I find it useful to catalogue.

subject: Daz's Combat Refusal

subject: Daz's Fireball

subject: Daz's fireball

subject: Daz's refusal to be extracted

source_quote: I am not gonna leave... I don't give a damn if you get paid... Not hiding. Not extracted. Not managed.

subject: death of Ilvara Mizzrym
fact: Ilvara Mizzrym was destroyed by a radiant guiding bolt, which triggered her final transformation into a spore cloud. Her death was not dignified; it resulted in a hazardous biological explosion.
source_quote: The bolt found her this time. Radiant light. Clean and bright and final. Ilvara — Zuggtmoy's instrument, the corrupted high priestess of House Mizzrym, the reason we had been prisoners in the first place — folded and went still, and then, because the Underdark does not allow even death to be dignified, she did not simply fall. She *erupted*. A cloud of poisonous spores, billowing outward from what had been a person.

subject: Destruction of the Heart Fungus

source_quote: I spent so much time creating this icon.

subject: Grygum

source_quote: Twenty-six points. We had not brought a gelatinous cube this far through the Underdark to lose him to biting insects conjured by a woman who had traded her dignity to a fungal demon lord.

subject: Jorlan’s Charge Against Ilvara

source_quote: He broke from position and charged toward her across the swarm-infested terrain, and the name that came out of him was not a battle cry.

subject: Thorin

subject: Thorin

subject: Tides Have Turned
fact: Zalthir declares 'The tides have turned' as Jorlan charges Ilvara, marking a narrative pivot from party versus villain to personal vendetta, accepted by the group as sufficient resolution.
source_quote: "The tides have turned."

subject: travel to Sloobludop
fact: Sloobludop is approximately eight days away via the Darklake.
source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: T'sarran soldier
fact: Another T'sarran soldier said 'And you don't have a Dispel Magic.'
source_quote: "And you don't have a Dispel Magic."

subject: T'sarran soldier
fact: Another T'sarran soldier said 'So I have to go through this. I don't know what else to tell you.'
source_quote: "So I have to go through this. I don't know what else to tell you."

subject: T'sarran soldier
fact: One T'sarran soldier said 'I thought you said this was going to be an easy kill.'
source_quote: "I thought you said this was going to be an easy kill."

subject: T'sarran soldiers
fact: The T'sarran soldiers were busy at the tunnel mouth having an argument that I can only describe as profoundly unhelpful given the circumstances.
source_quote: There's a category of failure I find almost aesthetically interesting — not the grand collapse, but the petty logistical one. They had the firepower. They had the numbers. What they did not have was Dispel Magic, and so they stood in the tunnel debating whether to charge while a 4th-level fireball was introduced into the conversation.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir accepted damage from the Heart Fungus while unable to close the distance to Ilvara.
source_quote: It found me. The blow was enormous — the kind of damage that lands differently when you have no immediate recourse...

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir chose not to approach Ilvara despite his monk training emphasizing proximity.
source_quote: I stayed where I was. Forty feet up. The frightened condition is not subtle — it is not a suggestion.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir decided to annoy Ilvara Mizzrym instead of engaging her directly.
source_quote: I'm just gonna try annoying her then.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir delivered two consecutive critical strikes against Ilvara Mizzrym.
source_quote: Crit. I do not celebrate at the table. But the second one surprised even me...

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir failed a DC-14 Wisdom saving throw against Ilvara’s psychological attack.
source_quote: Roll a DC-14 Wisdom saving throw. Well. That didn't work.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir looked at Ilvara and felt a fear that landed like a stone into still water, compelling him to stop moving toward her.
source_quote: And then she looked at him. And something in that look — something Zuggtmoy-deep, something that had nothing to do with Ilvara Mizzrym's personal opinion of Zalthir and everything to do with the demon lord wearing her face — *landed*. The fear dropped into him like a stone into still water.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noted the fear cleared at the end of his turn, as promised, without celebration.
source_quote: The fear cleared at the end of his turn, the way it had been promised to. He noted this without celebration.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir picked Ilvara up and used the Eldritch Claw Tattoo to wrap tentacles around her, hauling her forty feet into the air and dropping her.
source_quote: He had opened this fight by *picking Ilvara up*. Used the Eldritch Claw Tattoo to wrap tentacles around her, hauled her forty feet into the air, hit her twice in the ribs during the ascent, and dropped her.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir processed 'Are there 3 more unnamed creatures? 5 Dark Elves, it looks like? 5 Drow?' with his characteristic meditative calm and said 'That's awesome.'
source_quote: "Are there 3 more unnamed creatures?" "5 Dark Elves, it looks like? 5 Drow?" Zalthir processed this with his characteristic meditative calm. "That's awesome."

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir stood across the cavern and could not move toward Ilvara, filing it away and waiting.
source_quote: He watched from across the cavern and could not move toward her and filed it away and waited.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir teleported across the battlefield and hit the T'sarran mage once, killing him.
source_quote: He teleported across the battlefield — shadow-step, the distance closing in the space between one breath and the next — and hit the mage once, and that was enough.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir watched Ilvara mutter about Zuggtmoy, the bride, and chaos to come, and recognized her tone as one of genuine belief.
source_quote: She was still muttering. Something about Zuggtmoy. Something about the bride, and chaos, and the mayhem to come. She said it in the tone of someone who genuinely believed it, which was the worst kind.

subject: Zalthir's final realization
fact: Zalthir realized he was supposed to not be near Ilvara — not a question, but a rule, applied against his own interest.
source_quote: I am supposed to be trying to not be near her. Right. Not a question. Just the rule, stated plainly, applied against his own interest

subject: Zalthir's internal conflict
fact: Zalthir understood he must not close on Ilvara, a rule he enforced against his own instinct, rooted in the discipline of the Eldritch Claw Tattoo.
source_quote: The spirit of it was that he shouldn't close on her, and he knew the spirit of it, and so he didn't. The discipline is self-administered. Always has been.

subject: Zalthir's strike on the mage
fact: Zalthir teleported via shadow-step and delivered a single decisive blow to the T'sarran Mage, killing him instantly after the mage had already been weakened.
source_quote: He teleported across the battlefield — shadow-step, the distance closing in the space between one breath and the next — and hit the mage once, and that was enough.

subject: Zalthir's teleport strike
fact: Zalthir teleported across the battlefield using shadow-step and struck the T'sarran mage once, killing him instantly.
source_quote: He teleported across the battlefield — shadow-step, the distance closing in the space between one breath and the next — and hit the mage once, and that was enough.

subject: Drow Society
fact: Drow society is a brutal hierarchy that rewards physical beauty and punishes imperfection, leading to personal betrayals and emotional violence. Jorlan’s abandonment by Ilvara exemplifies this systemic cruelty.
source_quote: Ilvara had dumped Jorlan when he became Scarface, because Drow society rewards beauty and punishes everything else, because Drow society is a whole list of things I find exhausting.

subject: Drow society
fact: Drow society is structured around superficial values — rewarding beauty and punishing physical imperfection — which led Ilvara to abandon Jorlan when he became Scarface, and which Jorlan now rebels against by pursuing her.
source_quote: Drow society rewards beauty and punishes everything else

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym is a drow noble house aligned with Zuggtmoy, the Demon Lord of Fungal Nightmare. Ilvara Mizzrym serves as its high priestess, embodying its values of beauty, power, and corruption.
source_quote: Ilvara Mizzrym, high priestess of House Mizzrym, Zuggtmoy's beloved instrument, corrupted vessel of a demon lord of fungal nightmare.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym is the corrupted drow house to which Ilvara belonged — its legacy is one of demonic pacts and imprisonment, and its downfall is tied to the collapse of its high priestess and the spread of her fungal curse.
source_quote: Ilvara Mizzrym — Zuggtmoy's instrument, the corrupted high priestess of House Mizzrym, the reason we had been prisoners in the first place.

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym is the corrupted high priestess Ilvara’s former house, and the reason the party had been prisoners in the first place.
source_quote: Ilvara — Zuggtmoy's instrument, the corrupted high priestess of House Mizzrym, the reason we had been prisoners in the first place...

subject: House Mizzrym
fact: House Mizzrym was the corrupted high priestly lineage to which Ilvara Mizzrym belonged. Her transformation and death as Zuggtmoy’s instrument reflect the house’s deep entanglement with fungal demonic forces.
source_quote: Ilvara — Zuggtmoy's instrument, the corrupted high priestess of House Mizzrym...

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran deployed elite drow soldiers who were trained, armored, and contracted to resolve the crisis — they were stymied not by power but by the absence of Dispel Magic, resulting in a petty logistical failure that Daz finds aesthetically interesting.
source_quote: The matron mother of House T'sarran will hear about this.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran lost its last warrior and its mage in the confrontation; its matron mother is now aware of the party's actions and will likely respond, having been warned by the departing warrior.
source_quote: The last House T'sarran warrior... stepped back toward the tunnels... 'We will meet again.' I'll want to remember that name. The matron mother of House T'sarran would be hearing about this.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran suffered total loss — their mage dead, their guards incinerated, their last warrior standing amid the spore-choked ruin — and withdrew with a cold, calculated threat to return; Grygum noted the matron mother’s impending awareness as a future danger to be investigated.
source_quote: We will meet again. Enjoy your victory for the moment.

subject: House T'sarran
fact: House T'sarran’s matron mother will hear about the Fireball cast in the cavern — and that is probably going to matter later.
source_quote: The matron mother of House T'sarran will hear about this. She was not wrong. That is probably going to matter later. I filed it accordingly.

subject: Ilvara's cult
fact: Ilvara's cult has conjured a plague of insects and commands fungal servants, showing a pattern of using environmental hazards and divine fire in combat, and has traded allegiance to a fungal demon lord.
source_quote: Ilvara had conjured it at the cave entrance, a sphere of plague large enough to catch the whole middle ground between us — me, Daz, and, as I registered with a cold sinking feeling, Glabbagool.

subject: Lolth
fact: Lolth’s influence persisted through Asha Vandree’s prayers, which transformed Ilvara’s fall into a devotional narrative; the goddess is not defeated but reasserting herself through the reinterpretation of catastrophe, ensuring her cult remains active even in ruin.
source_quote: Prayers to Lolth, rising from the wreckage.

subject: Lolth
fact: The Spider Queen is the ideological anchor for Asha Vandree’s worldview and the basis for Daz’s fabricated identity, which functions as a social tool rather than a belief.
source_quote: Asha is a Lolth-devotee; she has a ready-made slot in her worldview for 'Lolth-aligned drow who are here to help.'

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: The drow city-state is the origin of Daz’s training, trauma, and identity, and the source of the societal structures he now rejects or manipulates.
source_quote: What Menzoberranzan made me and what the Underdark has cost me...

subject: the T'sarrans
fact: The T'sarrans were already gone from the battlefield, having withdrawn or fled after the conflict.
source_quote: The T'sarrans were already gone.

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy claimed Ilvara completely — not as a puppet, but as a living vessel of prophecy and corruption; her final moments were not a death but a venting of demonic essence, leaving behind spores and a lingering threat that reshaped the battlefield and the minds of those who witnessed it.
source_quote: Something Zuggtmoy-deep, something that had nothing to do with Ilvara Mizzrym's personal opinion of Zalthir and everything to do with the demon lord wearing her face.

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy is an ancient demon lord whose influence has taken hold of Ilvara, transforming her into a mouthpiece of chaos and prophecy, and whose presence has altered the psychological dynamics of the entire encounter.
source_quote: Something Zuggtmoy-deep, something that had nothing to do with Ilvara Mizzrym's personal opinion of Zalthir and everything to do with the demon lord wearing her face.

subject: bridge
fact: The bridge is referenced by Thorin as the structure he toppled, causing Ilvara and Jorlan to crash to the cavern floor.
source_quote: Thorin had already toppled the bridge, sent both of them crashing to the cavern floor...

subject: bridge collapse
fact: The bridge over Velkynvelve was destroyed by Thorin, sending Ilvara and Jorlan crashing to the cavern floor.
source_quote: Thorin had already toppled the bridge, sent both of them crashing to the cavern floor

subject: Bridge over Velkynvelve
fact: The bridge was once a strategic chokepoint, now reduced to rubble by Thorin’s force; its destruction marked the end of vertical control and the descent into chaotic, ground-level carnage, symbolizing the collapse of order in the fight.
source_quote: The bridge was rubble.

subject: cavern
fact: The cavern contains a collapsed heart fungus, a ruined bridge, a thick spore-choked silence, and a fading prophecy about a bride.
source_quote: The heart fungus was already a collapsed ruin — Thorin had seen to that in one devastating, almost insulting round... The bridge was rubble. The poisonous bloom was already beginning to thin and drift.

subject: Cavern
fact: The cavern is a vast, dark, fungal environment with elevated walkways, difficult terrain, and a central Heart Fungus, shaped by the DM as a bottleneck to force range and delay direct confrontation.
source_quote: The cavern was doing most of Ilvara's work for her — keeping us spread out, keeping me in particular at range from the thing I wanted to hit.

subject: Cavern
fact: The cavern is the site of a closing battle, with threats resolving from the periphery inward, the space shrinking as combatants fall and allies move to secure the remaining objectives.
source_quote: The fight was contracting toward its end the way fights do, the radius shrinking as each threat resolved.

subject: Cavern at Velkynvelve
fact: The cavern at Velkynvelve is now a ruined, spore-choked battlefield: bridge collapsed, fungus dead, mage and guards slain, Ilvara reduced to dissipating corruption; it is a place where victory is stained, silence is heavy, and the Underdark waits to correct optimism.
source_quote: The cavern settled into a thick, spore-choked silence.

subject: cavern floor
fact: The cavern floor is referenced by Thorin as the place where Ilvara and Jorlan hit after the bridge was toppled, and where the toxic bloom later spread.
source_quote: I watched them hit the cavern floor and thought: *still breathing*... The poisonous bloom was already beginning to thin and drift.

subject: Cavern of the Heart Fungus
fact: The cavern is a vast, dark space dominated by an enormous obscene mass of heart fungus on the floor; the monk operated from the ceiling while Ilvara and the fungus engaged from below.
source_quote: The cavernous space above the heart fungus was dark and vast and exactly the kind of silence I prefer to operate in.

subject: Cavern of the Heart Fungus
fact: The cavern is a vast, fungal-choked space dominated by the pulsing Heart Fungus, surrounded by difficult terrain and insect swarms. It functions as both battlefield and symbolic heart of Zuggtmoy’s influence.
source_quote: The cavernous space above the heart fungus was dark and vast and exactly the kind of silence I prefer to operate in.

subject: cavern silence
fact: The cavern settled into a thick, spore-choked silence after Ilvara's detonation, with only Asha’s prayers remaining.
source_quote: The cavern settled into a thick, spore-choked silence. The heart fungus was already a collapsed ruin... and somewhere in the settling quiet, Asha Vandree dropped to her knees and began murmuring prayers

subject: drow outpost elevation
fact: Dark Elves! I added, in a singing tone. The twelve days of Christmas. Five of them. Very irritated about the poison.
source_quote: Dark Elves!

subject: fungal cavern
fact: The fungal cavern is a complex, difficult-terrain environment dominated by the heart fungus, spore-choked air, and fungal minions, later transformed by the arrival of an insect swarm and the collapse of its central icon.
source_quote: Massive, pulsing, ringed with spore-choked air and difficult terrain between me and it

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a massive, pulsing, iconic fungal entity in the center of the cavern, resistant to common damage but doubly vulnerable to radiant damage, destroyed in one round by Thorin’s Dawnbringer.
source_quote: It actually is doubly not resistant to radiant damage. Dawnbringer was already in my hand. She'd been in my hand since we walked in. She's not the sort of sword that waits politely in a scabbard when there's something this obviously in need of being hit with radiant light.

subject: heart fungus ruin
fact: The heart fungus was destroyed by Thorin in one devastating round, reduced to a collapsed ruin.
source_quote: The heart fungus was already a collapsed ruin — Thorin had seen to that in one devastating, almost insulting round

subject: insect swarm at entrance
fact: An insect swarm remained active at the cavern entrance, requiring attention after the main combatants fell.
source_quote: Someone else was dealing with the insect swarm at the entrance.

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: Menzoberranzan is the drow city where Daz was trained as an Evoker — its culture values destructive magic as the only magic worth taking seriously, shaping his approach to spellcasting and his belief in the necessity of force.
source_quote: I am an Evoker, trained in Menzoberranzan where the destructive arts were considered the only magic worth taking seriously.

subject: ruined bridge and cavern floor
fact: The ruined bridge collapsed into a cavern floor saturated with Zuggtmoy’s corruption, now choked with lingering toxic spores and the wreckage of a battle that reshaped the local power dynamics.
source_quote: At the bottom of a ruined bridge with Zuggtmoy's rot flowering through everything she touches... The cavern settled into a thick, spore-choked silence.

subject: spore dispersion zone
fact: The area where Ilvara Mizzrym died became contaminated with a billowing cloud of poisonous spores, necessitating distance and caution. The spore cloud’s size and spread were noted as a tactical hazard.
source_quote: Not ideal," I said, immediately. "How big is the cloud?" I was glad I was standing back. This is the whole of my commentary on the death of Ilvara Mizzrym. Pragmatic wisdom. I was standing back. The cloud was noted. I took notes.

subject: The Cavern
fact: The cavern is a site of escalating chaos — it contains a persistent insect plague, a fungal spore cloud, a cracked bridge, and a tunnel mouth where elite soldiers debate rather than act — it is a space where death is undignified and strategy is undermined by poor preparation.
source_quote: The bridge cracked under her. Thorin's work. ... The tunnel mouth where elite drow soldiers were having an argument that I can only describe as profoundly unhelpful.

subject: the cavern
fact: The cavern is the site of multiple magical explosions, ongoing combat, and the lingering effects of plague and lightning, and it became very bright during the fireball.
source_quote: The cavern went very bright for a moment. The cavern floor was traversed by staggering combatants.

subject: the cavern
fact: The cavern was filled with a persistent insect bloom and a poison cloud, and the bridge cracked under Ilvara’s weight.
source_quote: The insect bloom still hanging in the air... the poison cloud's range... The bridge cracked under her.

subject: the tunnel mouth
fact: The tunnel mouth was where elite T'sarran drow soldiers stood debating whether to charge, stalled by a wall of insects and insufficient Dispel Magic.
source_quote: The T'sarran soldiers themselves, who were busy at the tunnel mouth having an argument that I can only describe as profoundly unhelpful... Elite drow soldiers... now stymied by a wall of insects and a mage with insufficient spell preparation.

subject: the Underdark
fact: The Underdark does not allow even death to be dignified — it forces corpses to erupt, not fall.
source_quote: because the Underdark does not allow even death to be dignified, she did not simply fall. She *erupted*.

subject: T'sarran retreat
fact: The last House T'sarran warrior stepped back toward the tunnels, declaring 'We will meet again' after witnessing Ilvara's demise and the mage's death.
source_quote: We will meet again," he said. "Enjoy your victory for the moment.

subject: tunnel mouth location
fact: The T'sarran soldiers themselves, who were busy at the tunnel mouth having an argument that I can only describe as profoundly unhelpful given the circumstances.
source_quote: The T'sarran soldiers themselves, who were busy at the tunnel mouth having an argument

subject: tunnels
fact: The tunnels are referenced by the last T'sarran warrior as the direction he stepped back toward after witnessing the defeat of his mage, guards, and Ilvara.
source_quote: The last House T'sarran warrior looked at all of it... and stepped back toward the tunnels without urgency. "We will meet again," he said.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is a hostile, ever-changing environment where alliances shift, minions vanish from memory, and even sentient creatures like Glabbagool are vulnerable to collateral damage, demanding constant adaptation.
source_quote: The Underdark keeps presenting me with long rooms. ... The Underdark is not kind to bystanders.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is a place where corruption is common, prophecy is accurate, and divine intervention is rare — forcing observers to rely on observation, positioning, and preemptive caution.
source_quote: I have seen enough of this Underdark to know better than to dismiss it.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is referenced by Grygum and Thorin as the setting where corruption, prophecy, and divine judgment are common, and where optimism is often corrected before the equation is finished.
source_quote: I have seen enough of this Underdark to know better than to dismiss it... The Underdark has a way of correcting your optimism before you even finish the equation.

subject: Underdark Cavern
fact: A confined, chittering, gas-filled cavern where combatants are trapped between Drow reinforcements, magical hazards, and internal conflict, serving as the stage for tactical absurdity and existential choices.
source_quote: ...the chittering wall of it while the poisonous gas did its work on both of us.

subject: Velkynvelve
fact: Velkynvelve is referenced by Thorin as the location where the bridge was toppled, the heart fungus destroyed, and the battle concluded with spores drifting and Asha praying in the dark.
source_quote: The bridge going down was my idea, technically... The fungus, at least, was mine... I stood there and let the quiet be quiet.

subject: Velkynvelve
fact: Velkynvelve was the cavern battlefield where the bridge collapsed, the fungus was destroyed, and spores spread — a sprawling, chaotic environment where the narrator lost situational awareness.
source_quote: The map spread out across half the cavern and the fight kept happening somewhere I wasn't.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: Biting Insects
fact: An inexhaustible swarm of aggressive insects forming a hazardous field that impedes combatants and contributes to the tactical chaos.
source_quote: ...a field of biting insects and what appears to be an inexhaustible supply of Drow reinforcements...

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Corrupted High Priestess
fact: A powerful, corrupted drow priestess engaged in active combat with Thorin, Grygum, and Zalthir, surrounded by biting insects and reinforced by Drow warriors.
source_quote: Thorin and Grygum and Zalthir are in active combat with a corrupted high priestess and a field of biting insects...

subject: Demonic Spore Cloud
fact: The spore cloud released by Ilvara’s death was a living hazard — toxic, airborne, and self-propagating; it was not merely a byproduct but an extension of Zuggtmoy’s will, punishing proximity and forcing retreat.
source_quote: A cloud of poisonous spores billowing through the cavern in every direction.

subject: drow count
fact: Five drow warriors are emerging from the cavern shadows.
source_quote: Five Drow, it looks like? 5 Drow?

subject: drow count
fact: Three Drow warriors. Crossbow formation. Tactical positions chosen in advance.
source_quote: Three Drow warriors. Crossbow formation. Tactical positions chosen in advance.

subject: drow reinforcement count
fact: Five drow warriors emerging from the cavern shadows.
source_quote: Five drow warriors emerging from the cavern shadows

subject: drow reinforcement count
fact: Three Drow warriors are stepping out of concealment with the particular ease of people who think they've caught something interesting in their sights.
source_quote: Three Drow warriors. Crossbow formation. Tactical positions chosen in advance.

subject: Drow Reinforcements
fact: Multiple drow warriors arriving in tactical formations, armed with crossbows and positioned to exploit surprise, now entangled in the same chaotic battlefield they were sent to control.
source_quote: Three Drow warriors. Crossbow formation. Tactical positions chosen in advance.

subject: Drow Warriors (5)
fact: Five drow warriors emerged from the cavern shadows, already inside the poison cloud’s range — they were tactical, armored, and prepared for combat, but were quickly neutralized by Daz’s sculpted Fireball.
source_quote: Five drow warriors emerging from the cavern shadows. ... The new arrivals were already inside the poison cloud's range.

subject: Eldritch Claw Tattoo
fact: The Eldritch Claw Tattoo manifests as fifteen feet of tentacular reach, used by Zalthir to restrain and assault Ilvara, but its power is nullified by the psychological fear it triggers in him.
source_quote: Used the Eldritch Claw Tattoo to wrap tentacles around her, hauled her forty feet into the air.

subject: five Drow warriors
fact: Five unnamed Drow warriors emerged from the cavern shadows, already within the poison cloud’s range, having made a dramatic entrance into a catastrophe they did not create, now reacting with irritation and confusion.
source_quote: Five drow warriors emerging from the cavern shadows. The insect bloom still hanging in the air. The new arrivals were already inside the poison cloud's range.

subject: Fungal Minions
fact: Fungal Minions are Ilvara’s thirteen-hit-point servants, instantly destroyed by the Insect Plague, whose deaths are later claimed as hers by the party, revealing the ambiguity of ownership in Underdark combat.
source_quote: The fallen fungal servants belonged to Ilvara, not to us. Of course they did.

subject: fungal servants
fact: Fungal minions loyal to Ilvara, now fallen and counted among her losses — distinct from the party’s own allies, their deaths triggering moral reckoning and spellcasting decisions.
source_quote: Not our minions. *Her* minions. The fallen fungal servants belonged to Ilvara, not to us. Of course they did.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient, gentle, luminously good-natured ooze companion who simply tries to participate in the ambient conversation of the battle — he survived twenty-six points of damage from Ilvara’s plague, making him an unexpected casualty of collateral magic.
source_quote: Our sentient, gentle, luminously good-natured ooze companion who had been, from what I could tell, simply trying to participate in the ambient conversation of the battle — had already taken twenty-six points of damage from Ilvara's plague and survived.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient, wobbling, gelatinous cube companion who survives twenty-six points of damage from Ilvara’s Insect Plague, and is treated by Grygum as a vulnerable being deserving of protection.
source_quote: Our faithful, wobbling, occasionally conversational gelatinous cube companion, who had been attempting to participate in the fight with the earnest commitment of someone who was very new to fighting and very sincere about it.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, the sentient, gentle, luminously good-natured ooze companion, had taken twenty-six points of damage from Ilvara's plague and survived.
source_quote: Glabbagool — our sentient, gentle, luminously good-natured ooze companion who had been, from what I could tell, simply trying to participate in the ambient conversation of the battle — had already taken twenty-six points of damage from Ilvara's plague and survived.

subject: Glabbagool inquiry
fact: Grygum's first real question after the spore cloud thinned was about Glabbagool, indicating its relevance to the aftermath.
source_quote: My first real question, once the cloud was thin enough to breathe through, was about Glabbagool.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a massive, iconic fungal entity at the center of the cavern, serving as both environmental hazard and symbolic centerpiece. It was destroyed in one round by Thorin’s Dawnbringer, despite extensive preparation by the DM.
source_quote: It was massive, pulsing, ringed with spore-choked air and difficult terrain between me and it — a whole careful geography of annoyance.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The heart fungus is a massive, sentient fungal entity that resides on the cavern floor; it attacked the monk from fifteen feet of reach, dealing significant bludgeoning and poison damage while the monk was immobilized by fear.
source_quote: It found me. The blow was enormous — the kind of damage that lands differently when you have no immediate recourse.

subject: heart fungus
fact: The heart fungus was a collapsed ruin before the battle, destroyed by Thorin in one devastating round while the observer stood idle with prepared abilities.
source_quote: The heart fungus was already a collapsed ruin — Thorin had seen to that in one devastating, almost insulting round, while I stood there with everything I'd prepared for it and nowhere to deploy it.

subject: heart fungus
fact: The heart fungus was a massive, pulsing, spore-choked entity with resistance to typical fungal vulnerabilities, but was doubly vulnerable to radiant damage and was destroyed in one round by Dawnbringer.
source_quote: It actually is doubly not resistant to radiant damage.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The heart fungus was a massive, slow-growing horror that took weeks to stat; Thorin destroyed it in two rounds, rendering it irrelevant and symbolizing the futility of elaborate environmental threats against overwhelming radiant force.
source_quote: Big pulsating horror that must have taken the DM weeks to stat out, and it folded before anyone else could touch it.

subject: insect plague
fact: A swarm of insects conjured by Ilvara, forming a wall of chittering fury that bypasses rational thought and targets flesh, currently hanging in the air and affecting both allies and new arrivals.
source_quote: A wall of noise, of biting, chittering fury, the kind of sound that bypasses the thinking part of the brain and goes straight to the older, smaller part that just says *run*.

subject: Insect Plague
fact: Insect Plague is a spell cast by Ilvara that manifests as a swarming, shrieking mass of insects that annihilates all organic life in its path, including fungal minions and Glabbagool.
source_quote: The swarm hit the cavern entrance like a wall of sound and motion — a biblical chittering that shredded the fungal minions instantly, all thirteen hit points of them, gone before they could do anything useful.

subject: Insect Plague
fact: The Insect Plague is a hazard that irritated Drow warriors and was neutralized by the shaped fireball, rendering them no longer irritated.
source_quote: The Drow warriors who had been irritated about the Insect Plague were no longer irritated about the Insect Plague

subject: Insect Plague
fact: The insect plague is a pervasive hazard that hangs in the air, damaging all who enter — it has already claimed twenty-six points of damage from Glabbagool and rendered multiple Drow warriors irrelevant by killing them outright.
source_quote: The insect bloom still hanging in the air. ... The Drow warriors who had been irritated about the Insect Plague were no longer irritated about the Insect Plague.

subject: Insect Plague Swarm
fact: The Insect Plague Swarm is a biblical chittering wall of insects conjured by Ilvara at the cavern entrance, instantly killing thirteen hit points of fungal minions and dealing twenty-six damage to Glabbagool.
source_quote: The swarm hit the cavern entrance like a wall of sound and motion — a biblical chittering that shredded the fungal minions instantly, all thirteen hit points of them, gone before they could do anything useful.

subject: Insect Swarm
fact: An insect swarm occupies the cavern entrance, now being dealt with by an unseen ally as the battle contracts toward resolution.
source_quote: Someone else was dealing with the insect swarm at the entrance.

subject: insect swarm
fact: An insect swarm summoned by Ilvara’s Insect Plague spell arrived unexpectedly, shredding all thirteen hit points of the fungal minions instantly and collateral-damaging Glabbagool.
source_quote: The swarm hit the cavern entrance like a wall of sound and motion

subject: Insect Swarm at Entrance
fact: An insect swarm lingered at the cavern entrance, later dealt with by an unnamed ally; it was a minor, persistent hazard that symbolized the encroaching corruption of the Underdark, now neutralized as the battle contracted toward its end.
source_quote: Someone else was dealing with the insect swarm at the entrance.

subject: spore cloud
fact: A cloud of poisonous spores erupted from Ilvara Mizzrym’s remains, billowing outward as a hazardous biological residue. The spores were the only physical manifestation left after her transformation and death.
source_quote: She *erupted*. A cloud of poisonous spores, billowing outward from what had been a person. A woman who had traded herself to a fungal demon lord, and what was left was biology, not identity. Not even a body. Just spores.

subject: the fungus
fact: The fungus, named Dawnbringer, was destroyed in one radiant strike — a pulsating horror that took the DM weeks to stat out and folded before anyone else could act.
source_quote: The fungus, at least, was mine. Clean and total. Dawnbringer lit the thing up from the first swing and it never got a second chance — big pulsating horror that must have taken the DM weeks to stat out, and it folded before anyone else could touch it.

subject: the spores
fact: The spores were a lethal environmental hazard that punished proximity, affecting multiple characters including the narrator and Zalthir.
source_quote: Spores everywhere — the kind of death that punishes you for being nearby. I caught some of it. Zalthir caught some of it.

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy, the fungal demon lord, was the entity to whom Ilvara Mizzrym had made a pact. She served as its instrument, and her final form — a spore cloud — was a direct manifestation of its corrupting influence.
source_quote: Ilvara — Zuggtmoy's instrument... A woman who had traded herself to a fungal demon lord...

subject: Zuggtmoy's rot
fact: Zuggtmoy's corruption manifested as a flowering rot through everything Ilvara touched, culminating in a massive toxic bloom of spores upon her death, venting demonic corruption all at once.
source_quote: Zuggtmoy's rot flowering through everything she touches... her body ruptured outward in a massive toxic bloom — a cloud of poisonous spores billowing through the cavern in every direction.

subject: Asha
fact: Asha was still praying in the dark, expecting to be answered, after the battle in Velkynvelve.
source_quote: Asha was still praying in the dark like she expected to be answered.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree believed Daz and the Duskryn sisters were traitors to Lolth until he smoothly inserted them into her existing framework as Lolth-aligned allies.
source_quote: Who are you? You must be traitors! Traitors to Lolth!... No, these are friends of Lolth, and they're here to help. The words came out smooth. No hesitation, no announcement, no explanation.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree dropped to her knees after Ilvara’s detonation and began murmuring prayers to Lolth, reshaping the witnessed destruction into theological material her goddess could claim.
source_quote: Asha Vandree dropped to her knees and began murmuring prayers, her voice the only sound left — words to Lolth, rising from the wreckage, already reshaping what she'd witnessed into something her goddess could use.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a devoted follower of Lolth who interprets all drow through the lens of her faith, readily accepting the fictional identity Daz maintains as consistent with Lolth-aligned intent.
source_quote: Who are you? You must be traitors! Traitors to Lolth!

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a zealot who immediately labeled the Duskryn sisters as traitors to Lolth — her rigid worldview was temporarily sustained by Daz’s performance of Lolth-follower identity, which he maintains with the momentum of consistent characterization rather than deception.
source_quote: Who are you? You must be traitors! Traitors to Lolth!

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is referenced by Grygum as the one who dropped to her knees and began murmuring prayers to Lolth, reshaping what she'd witnessed into something her goddess could use.
source_quote: Somewhere in the settling quiet, Asha Vandree dropped to her knees and began murmuring prayers, her voice the only sound left — words to Lolth, rising from the wreckage, already reshaping what she'd witnessed into something her goddess could use.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is referenced by Thorin as the one who was still praying in the dark like she expected to be answered, and whom Thorin had seen stranger things answered.
source_quote: Asha was still praying in the dark like she expected to be answered. Maybe she would be. I've seen stranger things answered.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree knelt in the aftermath of Ilvara’s death and began praying to Lolth, reshaping the tragedy into theology, turning witnessed corruption into a foundation for future worship — a silent act of resilience and ideological continuation that Grygum noted as something to watch.
source_quote: Prayers to Lolth, rising from the wreckage.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a former Menzoberranzan operative now operating in the Underdark, maintaining a fictional Lolth-follower identity to navigate alliances, and refusing to prioritize survival over participation in combat despite contractual pressures.
source_quote: I am not gonna leave. Everyone here... to fight for me without me also participating. I don't give a damn if you get paid.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a member of the party known for his cheekbones, monologues, and range-based tactics. He is contrasted with Zalthir and Thorin as the archetype of theatricality and distance, often serving as a foil to their directness.
source_quote: I do not, as a rule, enjoy monologue. I leave that to Daz, who has the cheekbones for it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a party member who enjoys monologue and possesses cheekbones suited for dramatic delivery, contrasted against Zalthir’s aversion to speech and Thorin’s preference for action.
source_quote: I do not, as a rule, enjoy monologue. I leave that to Daz, who has the cheekbones for it.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is referenced by Thorin as the one who fired an empowered fireball through the last T'sarran mage, singeing him at the edges.
source_quote: Daz had already run an empowered fireball through him; the man was singed at the edges and blinking with the stunned expression of someone who had entered this fight expecting an easy kill and received instead a detailed education in why that assumption was wrong.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the feared mage of the Ember Vanguard, standing in the smoke of his own fireball, surrounded by people who are fighting because he refused to leave — he chose not to hide, not to be extracted, not to be managed, and found in that refusal what purpose feels like.
source_quote: The feared mage of the Ember Vanguard, standing in the smoke of his own fireball, surrounded by people who were fighting because he refused to leave. I find, somewhat to my own surprise, that this is what purpose feels like.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz obliterated the T'sarran mage with an empowered fireball, demonstrating lethal precision; his role in the aftermath was to explain why the chaos was acceptable, likely to others still reeling from the battle’s brutality.
source_quote: Why exactly this was all fine.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz refused to hide, declared he would not leave others to fight for him without participating, and cast a shaped Fireball to protect allies while destroying enemies.
source_quote: I am not gonna leave. Everyone here... to fight for me without me also participating. I don't give a damn if you get paid. The best way for you to get paid, then, is to continue the fight and prevent all of us from dying... I cast Fireball in a shaped arc around everything I wanted to keep.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was probably explaining to someone why the events of the battle were all fine.
source_quote: Daz was probably explaining to someone why exactly this was all fine.

subject: Daz
fact: That's the thing about Shield — it's a reaction, which means the body decides before the mind does.
source_quote: That's the thing about Shield — it's a reaction, which means the body decides before the mind does.

subject: Daz
fact: Three Drow warriors. Crossbow formation. Tactical positions chosen in advance. Someone prepared for this.
source_quote: *Three Drow warriors. Crossbow formation. Tactical positions chosen in advance. Someone prepared for this.*

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient gelatinous cube companion who earnestly but ineffectually participates in combat. He survived twenty-six points of damage from Ilvara’s Insect Plague, becoming a symbol of unintended collateral damage in the Underdark’s brutal conflicts.
source_quote: Twenty-six points of damage. The grey ooze took twenty-six points of damage from a spell he had nothing to do with, while he was hovering at the edge of the chaos doing his best to look like he was following the conversation.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient gelatinous cube companion who participated in combat with earnest sincerity, survived a 26-point insect swarm attack, and is now trembling in the aftermath — a vulnerable ally whose survival was not anticipated by the party’s logistics.
source_quote: Glabbagool. Twenty-six points of damage, I was told. The cube had survived, churning and trembling in the swarm.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a sentient, gentle, luminously good-natured ooze companion who survived twenty-six points of damage from Ilvara's plague and continues to endure the hazards of the cavern.
source_quote: Glabbagool had been, from what I could tell, simply trying to participate in the ambient conversation of the battle

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool, a sentient grey ooze attempting to participate in the battle, took twenty-six points of radiant damage from the Insect Plague spell despite having no role in the conflict, leaving him injured but alive and emotionally marginalized.
source_quote: Oh, how about Glabbagool?

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum acknowledges the difficulty of bookkeeping companions in the Underdark due to an expanding roster.
source_quote: We used to have so many people traveling with us, I forgot.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum delivered the final Guiding Bolt to Ilvara, recognizing her as irredeemably corrupted by Zuggtmoy; he acted not out of vengeance but divine pragmatism, positioning himself safely to avoid the resulting spore explosion, and filed away the threat of House T'sarran's matron mother and the mystery of Glabbagool.
source_quote: Not ideal, how big is the cloud, glad I was standing back.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a cleric who prioritizes compassion and accountability. He was the first to voice concern for Glabbagool during the Insect Plague, offered Revivify to restore fallen minions, and reflected on the logistical chaos of tracking allies and enemies in the Underdark.
source_quote: "Oh, how about Glabbagool?" That was me. That was the question I asked first, before I assessed my own position...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a party member who prioritizes the safety of Glabbagool over tactical concerns, uses Revivify to consider restoring fallen minions, and is acutely aware of the shifting loyalties and bookkeeping failures of Underdark companionship.
source_quote: Oh, how about Glabbagool? ... If anybody is too saddened by the loss of any of our minions, I do have a Revivify spell that I could use to bring one of them back.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is moving forward after the primary threats have fallen, contributing to the final contraction of the battle.
source_quote: Behind Zalthir, someone — Grygum, probably — was already moving forward.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who filed Asha Vandree’s prayers under 'watch this space.'
source_quote: Whatever theology she was building out of this moment, I filed it under *watch this space.*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who filed the threat from the T'sarran warrior under 'remember that name' because a threat delivered without heat is more credible.
source_quote: A threat delivered without heat is always more credible than one made in anger. I'll want to remember that name.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who fired Guiding Bolt at Ilvara, causing her body to rupture outward in a massive toxic bloom of poisonous spores.
source_quote: The bolt left my hand. It lanced across the cavern floor in a concentrated column of radiant light and found her where she stood. She did not die quietly. She detonated. Her body ruptured outward in a massive toxic bloom — a cloud of poisonous spores billowing through the cavern in every direction...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who noted that Bahamut does not favor spectatorship and that he gets credit for positioning, not radiance.
source_quote: Bahamut does not, in my experience, favor spectatorship... Bahamut gets the credit for the radiance. I get credit for the positioning.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who noted that the last T'sarran warrior said, 'Enjoy your victory for the moment,' and filed it as a threat to be remembered.
source_quote: "Enjoy your victory for the moment." I took note of that too.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who said, 'A threat delivered without heat is always more credible than one made in anger.'
source_quote: A threat delivered without heat is always more credible than one made in anger.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who said, 'Bahamut and I understand each other,' regarding the division of credit for radiance and positioning.
source_quote: Bahamut gets the credit for the radiance. I get credit for the positioning. We understand each other, Bahamut and I.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who said, 'I believe I should find out who that is before she finds out who we are.'
source_quote: I believe I should find out who that is before she finds out who we are.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who said, 'I had so much planned for the fungus.'
source_quote: *Boy, I had so much planned for the fungus.*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who said, 'I have never once received a divine message that said *wait this one out, it's interesting.*'
source_quote: I have never once received a divine message that said *wait this one out, it's interesting.*

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who said, 'I think I'm still going to go ahead and attack them,' after being amused by the Jorlan-Ilvara drama.
source_quote: I'm amused by the Jorlan-Ilvara drama, I thought. But I think I'm still going to go ahead and attack them.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who said, 'I took mental notes. It's what I do.'
source_quote: I took mental notes. It's what I do.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who said, 'I'm amused by the Jorlan-Ilvara drama.'
source_quote: I'm amused by the Jorlan-Ilvara drama, I thought.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who said, 'One turn is a long time when you have nothing to do in it.'
source_quote: One turn is a long time when you have nothing to do in it.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who said, 'The entertainment of watching enemies tear at each other is free.'
source_quote: The entertainment of watching enemies tear at each other is free.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by himself as the one who thought, 'not ideal, how big is the cloud, glad I was standing back,' after Ilvara detonated.
source_quote: Not ideal, I thought, immediately practical again. How big is the cloud? I was glad I was standing back.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observed that Asha's characterization of Daz as an insane mage who converted to Lolthism was 'accurately described,' with his steady, clear-eyed precision.
source_quote: Grygum, at some point in this sequence, observed that the situation was 'accurately described' by Asha's characterization of me as an insane mage who had converted to Lolthism. He meant it kindly. Or as kindly as Grygum observes anything, which is with the steady, clear-eyed precision of a man keeping accurate records.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observes events with the steady, record-keeping precision of a man who treats reality as data, and accepts Daz’s fabricated identity as accurately described despite its falsehood.
source_quote: The situation was 'accurately described' by Asha's characterization of me as an insane mage who had converted to Lolthism.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum observes with the steady, clear-eyed precision of a man keeping accurate records — he noted that Asha’s characterization of Daz as an insane mage who converted to Lolthism was 'accurately described,' revealing his detached, factual lens on the unfolding fiction.
source_quote: The situation was 'accurately described' by Asha's characterization of me as an insane mage who had converted to Lolthism.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum offered blunt, helpful commentary throughout the encounter, asserting that the heart fungus is not resistant to swords and later acknowledging its aesthetic value after its death.
source_quote: It's not resistant to swords.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum prioritizes protecting the vulnerable, even if they are non-traditional companions like gelatinous cubes.
source_quote: Bahamut rewards the protection of the vulnerable. I'm not certain gelatinous cubes were what the Platinum Dragon had in mind. But I took notes on the principle...

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum thought of the Guiding Bolt as administrative when it worked, but in this case it felt like the light had been waiting.
source_quote: There is a version of Guiding Bolt that I think of as administrative — you point it, it works, enemy takes radiant damage, case closed. And then there is the other version, the one that happens when everything has led to this particular moment and the light in your hand feels like it has been waiting.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum's bolt found its target, and Grygum was likely checking on Glabbagool after the battle.
source_quote: Grygum's bolt found her. Somewhere behind me, Grygum was probably checking on Glabbagool.

subject: Gustatus
fact: Gustatus expressed personal affection for the heart fungus, offering condolences on its behalf and affirming its visual and emotional significance to the party.
source_quote: I liked it very much, Gustatus.

subject: Gustatus
fact: Gustatus is the Dungeon Master, who designed the Heart Fungus as a beloved icon, and who experiences quiet regret when it is destroyed too quickly by radiant damage.
source_quote: I spent so much time creating this icon. ... "I liked it very much, Gustatus."

subject: I
fact: I am an Evoker, trained in Menzoberranzan where the destructive arts were considered the only magic worth taking seriously.
source_quote: An Evoker — and I am an Evoker, trained in Menzoberranzan where the destructive arts were considered the only magic worth taking seriously — learns to carve exceptions into area spells.

subject: I
fact: I find, somewhat to my own surprise, that this is what purpose feels like.
source_quote: I find, somewhat to my own surprise, that this is what purpose feels like.

subject: I
fact: I have been maintaining a Lolth-follower identity with Asha Vandree for long enough that the fiction has its own momentum — you learn to stop thinking of it as lying and start thinking of it as consistent characterization.
source_quote: I have been maintaining a Lolth-follower identity with Asha Vandree for long enough that the fiction has its own momentum — you learn to stop thinking of it as lying and start thinking of it as consistent characterization.

subject: I
fact: I know what's real. I know what I've left behind and what I haven't and what Menzoberranzan made me and what the Underdark has cost me and what I believe now, privately, about slavery and free people and the basis of any society.
source_quote: I know what's real. I know what I've left behind and what I haven't and what Menzoberranzan made me and what the Underdark has cost me and what I believe now, privately, about slavery and free people and the basis of any society.

subject: I
fact: I remained exactly where I had said I would remain. Not hiding. Not extracted. Not managed.
source_quote: I remained exactly where I had said I would remain. Not hiding. Not extracted. Not managed.

subject: I
fact: I was amused by the Jorlan-Ilvara drama — the romantic betrayal, the scarring, the fury, the way he had broken from us to pursue her through an active insect plague.
source_quote: I was amused by the Jorlan-Ilvara drama. I want to be clear about that. The romantic betrayal. The scarring. The fury. The way he had broken from us to pursue her through an active insect plague. It was genuinely interesting. I filed it, appreciated it, and continued.

subject: I
fact: I was glad I was standing back. This is the whole of my commentary on the death of Ilvara Mizzrym. Pragmatic wisdom. I was standing back. The cloud was noted. I took notes.
source_quote: I was glad I was standing back. This is the whole of my commentary on the death of Ilvara Mizzrym. Pragmatic wisdom. I was standing back. The cloud was noted. I took notes.

subject: Ilvara

source_quote: Ilvara — Zuggtmoy's instrument, the corrupted high priestess of House Mizzrym, the reason we had been prisoners in the first place — folded and went still, and then, because the Underdark does not allow even death to be dignified, she did not simply fall. She *erupted*. A cloud of poisonous spores, billowing outward from what had been a person. A woman who had traded herself to a fungal demon lord, and what was left was biology, not identity. Not even a body. Just spores.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a dying but prophetic figure, channeling Zuggtmoy’s will through her, filling the battlefield with chaotic prophecy rather than plea or surrender, even as she is physically broken.
source_quote: Vengeance. Zuggtmoy. The bride.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a former ally turned antagonist who survived a forty-foot drop, continues to conjure divine fire, and has lost her dignity to a fungal demon lord, now fighting with focused fury despite structural collapse.
source_quote: Ilvara, battered from her forty-foot drop courtesy of Zalthir's extraordinary grip-and-release approach to aerial combat, was still moving, still conjuring, still calling down divine fire on Daz and Nym Duskryn with the focused fury of someone who had not yet accepted that this was over.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is referenced by Grygum as the one who was already something other than the woman she had been, with corruption working on her for a long time.
source_quote: She was already something other than the woman she had been. The corruption had been working on her for a long time.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is referenced by Zalthir as the one who looked at him with a Zuggtmoy-deep expression, something that had nothing to do with her personal opinion of Zalthir and everything to do with the demon lord wearing her face.
source_quote: And then she looked at him. And something in that look — something Zuggtmoy-deep, something that had nothing to do with Ilvara Mizzrym's personal opinion of Zalthir and everything to do with the demon lord wearing her face — *landed*.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is referenced by Zalthir as the one who was still howling, her voice ragged with desperation, filling the space with prophecy rather than offers.
source_quote: Ilvara was still on the far side of the cavern, still howling, her voice ragged with the particular desperation of someone who has run out of futures but not yet run out of throat. *Vengeance. Zuggtmoy. The bride.* All of it tumbling out between strikes and retreats.

subject: Ilvara
